profile.name: Malak Elgwaely
profile.intro: Computer Science student at Alexandria University, interested in backend development, machine learning, and the practical side of building software. I like figuring out why something works — then making it work better.
profile.about: I’m Malak, a Computer Science student at Alexandria University. I’m drawn to the parts of technology that need both patience and problem-solving: understanding a system, breaking a big problem into smaller ones, and building a solution that someone can actually use.
profile.aboutMore: My learning hasn’t happened only behind a laptop. Between technical programs, university projects, volunteering, and community events, I’ve learned that I enjoy taking responsibility, working with different people, and being useful where I can. I’m currently exploring backend development and machine learning, while keeping room for the things that challenge me outside code.

projects.title: LifeOS
projects.summary: A personal operating system for goals, projects, tasks, notes, and daily workflows.
projects.description: A shareable productivity dashboard designed to bring different areas of life into one organized workspace. Built with a focus on clear workflows, responsive UI, and persistent personal data.
projects.challenge: Designing a flexible system that keeps goals, tasks, projects, and daily actions connected without overwhelming the user.

projects.title: Protein Max Gallery
projects.summary: A product-focused gallery website built around a clean and responsive browsing experience.

projects.challenge: Keeping the product presentation clear and consistent across screen sizes while making the browsing experience simple.

projects.title: Delivery Delay Prediction
projects.summary: A data analysis and decision-tree workflow using 10,000+ delivery records.
projects.description: A project exploring delivery performance through data cleaning, preprocessing, factor analysis, and a conceptual decision-tree prediction workflow.
